title: Runtime Budget and Agent-Cap Enforcement Audit
gradingCriteria: Identifies that a journal cache hit (ctx.journal.next(key).hit) returns the cached result before the cap and budget checks, so cached replays are exempt from both MAX_AGENTS and the budget ceiling (no Codex spawn).
States the agent cap is enforced by `++ctx.counters.launched > MAX_AGENTS` (1000) which counts only live spawns and throws 'agent cap reached' — cached replays do not increment it.
States the budget ceiling check `ctx.budget.remaining() <= 0` throws 'budget exhausted' and is deliberately NOT journaled, so a resume with more budget re-runs that agent.

Explains the budget check is performed inside ctx.sem.run AFTER acquiring a concurrency slot so completed agents' token spend is visible; at concurrency 1 this enforces the ceiling exactly, at higher concurrency it bounds overshoot to the in-flight set rather than admitting the whole fan-out.

Distinguishes the three outcomes correctly: budget/cap conditions throw; abort (ctx.signal.aborted) and stop/admission paths return null; only a normal completed outcome is recorded to the journal (and not when aborted).

Grounds the answer in budget.ts (remaining() is Infinity when total is null, so an unset budget never refuses) and journal.ts (agentKey folds model/effort/sandbox/schema/etc. into the cache key, and next() replays per-key occurrences in order), referencing concurrency from scheduler.ts.

Reports running the verification commands (bun test and `bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts lint packages/core/workflows/migrate.mjs`) and/or rg for the literal error strings, rather than reasoning purely from the file names.
